name: toili

attributes.attribute: a Welsh ghostly funeral train that foretells death

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The toili is a Welsh folkloric figure. At night a funeral appeared to move through a village, the villagers walking slowly behind a coffin toward the graveyard. Yet all those villagers were safe at home, for the line was only the toili, a ghostly funeral. People with the Second Sight could sometimes see it by day as well. The toili was a sign that a death was close. Anyone swept into its parade would die, so the wise turned aside when it passed.

okr.objective: Record the Welsh figure of the toili.
key_results: The toili appears as a ghostly funeral passing through a village at night
Those with Second Sight could sometimes see it by day
Its appearance warned that a death was near
Anyone swept into its parade would die
